$what: Every licence family the installed dependency tree may carry, and a disposition for each that is not a plain permissive licence. §11.7's dependency clause, and §10's Transfer Ownership: this inventory is what the client inherits.
$checkedBy: tools/gate/test/licences.test.mjs, which enumerates the installed pnpm store and fails on a licence family that is in neither map. A new dependency with an unlisted licence reddens the gate rather than arriving unexamined.
$whyNotAList: A per-PACKAGE list would go stale at every `pnpm install` and would differ by platform -- `lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu` and `@img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64` are optional platform binaries and a macOS clone resolves different ones. A per-LICENCE-FAMILY list is platform-robust: a new platform binary carries the same licence as its siblings, and a genuinely new licence is what wants a human.
$measured: 2026-10-31 on linux-x64, Node 22.23.4, pnpm 12.16.1: 229 installed packages. The counts below are that measurement and are NOT asserted, because the total varies with the platform's optional dependencies; what IS asserted is that every licence seen appears here.

(MIT OR CC0-1.0).note: A DUAL licence, and both halves are permissive, so the OR costs nothing: MIT needs attribution in the distributed copy and CC0-1.0 needs nothing at all. Arrived at Task 9 with the pinned Lighthouse CLI (`lighthouse@13.5.0`), which is a DEVELOPMENT dependency and a measurement tool: nothing it brings reaches the product, and `type-fest` ships type declarations only -- no runtime code in any bundle. Recorded as its own family rather than folded into MIT, because the string a scanner reads is the string this inventory must carry.

Apache-2.0.note: attribution plus a patent grant; no copyleft

BlueOak-1.0.0.note: OSI-approved permissive, plain-language. ⚠ ARRIVED WITH THIS TASK'S OWN minimatch OVERRIDE: minimatch 11 relicensed from ISC to Blue Oak, so closing GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 introduced a licence family the tree did not previously carry. Dispositioned rather than discovered later: it imposes no obligation this project does not already meet.

MIT.note: no obligation beyond attribution in the distributed copy

MIT-0.note: MIT with the attribution requirement removed

MPL-2.0.reach: a BUILD-TIME dependency of Tailwind v4. It parses and minifies CSS during `next build` and ships no code to a browser.
MPL-2.0.obligation: file-level copyleft: MPL-2.0 requires the SOURCE of any modified MPL file to be made available. It does not reach a work that merely uses it, and §2 of the licence is explicit that linking does not create a derivative work.
MPL-2.0.disposition: ACCEPTED. No MPL file is modified, forked or vendored -- it is consumed as a published npm package at a pinned version, so the obligation is discharged by the upstream project's own published source. Nothing MPL-licensed reaches the product's runtime at all.

LGPL-3.0-or-later.reach: a transitive optional dependency of `sharp`, itself reached through Next.js's image optimiser. A BUILD-TIME and server-side native binary; no part of it is served to a browser.
LGPL-3.0-or-later.obligation: LGPL permits use by a work under any licence provided the LGPL component stays replaceable -- which a dynamically-loaded prebuilt binary in `node_modules` is by construction. Distributing a MODIFIED libvips would require publishing that modification.
LGPL-3.0-or-later.disposition: ACCEPTED, with the condition written down rather than remembered: the binary is consumed unmodified and unbundled. ⚠ IF A FUTURE TASK PRODUCES A SINGLE-FILE OR STATICALLY-LINKED ARTEFACT containing it, this disposition no longer holds and the LGPL's relinking requirement has to be answered. Next.js 15's output is a Node server plus static assets, so that does not arise today.

CC-BY-4.0.reach: a BUILD-TIME data set, reached through `next` and `browserslist`. It is a database of browser-support facts, not code, and is read to decide which CSS and JS transforms to apply.
CC-BY-4.0.obligation: attribution for the DATA. Creative Commons' own FAQ is explicit that CC licences are not intended for software; here the subject genuinely is data.
CC-BY-4.0.disposition: ACCEPTED. The data is not redistributed: it is read at build time and nothing derived from it is published as a data set. Attribution is carried by this file, which §10 hands to the client with the repository.

CC0-1.0.reach: a BUILD-TIME data set reached through the CSS tooling.
CC0-1.0.obligation: none. CC0 is a dedication to the public domain.
CC0-1.0.disposition: ACCEPTED, and listed rather than folded into `permissive` because CC0 is a dedication and not a licence, so a reader looking for the obligation should find the answer stated.

refused.$note: Licence families that must NEVER appear. Listed so the refusal is a decision taken in advance rather than an argument had under pressure when a dependency arrives.
refused.GPL-2.0: strong copyleft reaching the whole work; incompatible with a proprietary delivery to a client
refused.AGPL-3.0: as above, and extends to network use -- which is exactly what this product is
refused.SSPL-1.0: not OSI-approved; its service clause reaches an entire deployment
refused.UNLICENSED: no grant at all; using it is simply infringement
